business_process: Online and app ticket sales (own events)
description: Event pages, seat selection, cart, and checkout on the web and mobile app for the company's own events (about 21 million tickets a year)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Revenue and fan trust: about $5.5 million of own-event ticket sales on an average day and 3 to 4 times that on peak on-sale days; orders and seat holds must not be lost or double-sold
manual_workaround: Pause sales and post a status message; extend presales; box office sells from printed seat maps only for same-day shows
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; edge, WAF, and bot management provider; tokenization and vault provider; two processors
quantified_impact_basis: About 35% of a day's own-event sales are not recovered after a full-day outage (about $1.9 million) plus about $0.5 million of service fees
acquired_venue_dependency: None (AV-01 to AV-06 sell online through the platform since 2026-04)
single_points_of_failure: Single edge and bot management provider; single tokenization provider

description: Payment fields, agent payment page, tokenization, and authorization routing to two processors for every card-not-present sale on the platform
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every online, app, and phone sale for own and client events stops without it; PCI DSS cardholder data environment; card-on-file tokens needed for refunds and chargebacks
manual_workaround: No manual card-not-present fallback. Reserve-now-pay-later holds for presales up to 24 hours (client opt-in)
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-01; SYS-04; SYS-05 (Cloud A CDE accounts)
dependent_third_parties: Tokenization and vault provider; processor 1 (about 70% of authorizations); processor 2 (about 30%); acquirer
dependent_people_or_facilities: Payments engineering; Director of Payments and PCI Compliance
quantified_impact_basis: Stops BP-01 and BP-07 together: about $12.6 million of gross sales on an average day, about 35% not recovered (about $4.4 million), plus client service credits of about $0.5 million
single_points_of_failure: Single tokenization and vault provider (tokens are not portable)

description: Scheduled on-sales for arena and amphitheater tours and festivals, with a virtual queue, bot defense, and posted ticket limits
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A failed major on-sale must be rescheduled with the artist and announced publicly; bots buy inventory if protection is off; about 140 high-demand on-sales a year
manual_workaround: Pause the queue and hold inventory; reschedule the on-sale with the artist's agreement; never reopen without bot protection
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (queue and bot defense services); SYS-02; SYS-05 (Cloud A)
dependent_third_parties: Edge, WAF, and bot management provider; Cloud provider A
dependent_people_or_facilities: Ticketing operations; Director of Fraud and Bot Defense
quantified_impact_basis: Peak on-sale day: about $18 million gross in the first 4 hours of a major tour on-sale; a rescheduled on-sale costs about $1.5 million (media, artist relations, staffing) and about $4.5 million of sales shift to resellers or are lost
single_points_of_failure: Single edge and bot management provider

business_process: Event-day entry and access control scanning
description: Rotating-barcode digital tickets scanned at gates by about 7,500 handheld scanners and turnstiles; about 3,500 event days a year
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Crowd safety at gates: a 20,000-seat amphitheater admits most attendees in 60 to 90 minutes; queues outside gates become a safety hazard within an hour
manual_workaround: Scanners switch to offline mode with the cached ticket list (synced 30 minutes before doors); visual checks of printed manifests for will-call
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (access control service); SYS-06 (venue networks); SYS-07 (scanners)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Gate staff; venue security; 36 venues and 3 festival sites
quantified_impact_basis: A 1-hour failure at doors on a busy night (about 20 events, 180,000 attendees): delayed starts, overtime, and refunds for missed sets, about $1.2 million
acquired_venue_dependency: AV-01 to AV-06 use the platform's scanners since 2026-04 but on single-carrier internet
single_points_of_failure: Venue internet circuit at single-carrier venues

description: Walk-up and will-call sales at 36 venue box offices on P2PE devices (legacy readers at AV-01 to AV-06)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Mostly same-day sales and will-call; about 4% of own-event tickets
manual_workaround: Will-call from printed manifests; direct buyers to the app; cash where the venue accepts it
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-03 (box office devices); SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: P2PE solution provider; legacy POS vendor (AV venues)
quantified_impact_basis: About 4% of own-event sales, mostly recovered through the app; staff idle time
acquired_venue_dependency: Yes: AV-01 to AV-06 box offices use legacy POS terminals

description: Stands, bars, and merchandise stalls on cloud POS with P2PE devices (about 31 million card sales a year); most venues are cashless
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Event-day revenue is lost for good if stands cannot sell during the show; about $2.2 million on an average day
manual_workaround: Cloud POS offline mode queues card sales for up to 4 hours (vendor setting, within acquirer risk limits); open cash-accepting stands where the venue allows cash
dependent_third_parties: Cloud POS vendor; P2PE solution provider; processor 1
dependent_people_or_facilities: Food and beverage staff; merchandise partners
quantified_impact_basis: About $0.8 billion a year of food, beverage, and merchandise sales; about $2.2 million on an average day, most of it not recoverable
acquired_venue_dependency: Yes: AV-01 to AV-06 stands use legacy POS terminals

description: Ticket sales, box office, and access control for about 340 client venues and promoters on client-branded sites (about 31 million tickets a year)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Client contracts: 99.9% monthly availability with service credits; clients are the merchants of record and depend on the platform for every sale
manual_workaround: Clients pause sales and post notices; no client fallback platform
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; edge, WAF, and bot management provider; tokenization and vault provider; processors
quantified_impact_basis: About $7.1 million of client gross sales on an average day: lost service fees about $0.6 million plus service credits up to $1.4 million per day under client agreements
single_points_of_failure: Single edge and bot management provider; single tokenization provider

business_process: Contact center sales and patron support
description: Phone sales, refunds, and patron support (about 6.5 million contacts a year) at the in-house center and the outsourced overflow center
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Phone sales are about 2% of orders; event-change and refund surges follow cancellations and weather
manual_workaround: Route callers to the app and web help center; in-house center absorbs priority calls; overflow center paused
dependent_systems: SYS-09; SYS-01; SYS-02 (agent payment page); SYS-04
dependent_third_parties: Cloud contact center platform; outsourced overflow contact center
quantified_impact_basis: Lost phone sales (about $0.3 million) plus overtime and callbacks

business_process: Event settlement with artists, promoters, and venue owners
description: Show-night settlement of ticket, fee, and merchandise revenue; about 5,400 settlements a year
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Artists expect settlement on show night but accept next-day settlement; contract terms set the outer limit
manual_workaround: Settle from platform exports and stand reports in spreadsheets with dual review; pay by wire next day
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime, late-payment penalties under some artist agreements, and artist relations
acquired_venue_dependency: Yes: AV-01 to AV-06 settle from legacy POS reports

description: CCTV (about 8,600 cameras), door access control, weapons screening, radio dispatch, and mass notification at 36 venues
process_owner: Vice President, Venue Security and Safety
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Life safety: an event cannot continue without screening, video coverage of crowds, and the ability to announce evacuation
manual_workaround: Manual screening posts with handheld wands; additional security staff on foot; public address announcements; stop entry if screening fails
dependent_third_parties: CCTV and video management vendor; weapons screening vendor; security staffing contractors
dependent_people_or_facilities: Venue security teams; local police liaison
quantified_impact_basis: Cancellation or delayed doors at an affected venue (about $0.6 million per arena event) plus extra staffing
acquired_venue_dependency: Yes: AV-01 to AV-06 have stand-alone CCTV recorders
single_points_of_failure: Vendor cloud management for screening systems

description: Building management (HVAC, lighting, power), elevators, and life safety interfaces at 36 venues
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Indoor venues cannot hold events without ventilation and lighting; life safety systems run independently by code
manual_workaround: Manual control at the plant; building engineers on site; cancel the event if conditions are unsafe
quantified_impact_basis: Cancellation of 1 to 2 indoor events on an average day
acquired_venue_dependency: Partial: two AV venues use an integrator-managed controller
single_points_of_failure: Shared OT network segments at 14 venues

description: Venue-owned lighting, audio, video walls, and broadcast feeds
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Touring productions bring their own consoles; venue systems matter for house shows and video boards
manual_workaround: Touring crew equipment; static house lighting
quantified_impact_basis: Degraded shows and sponsor make-goods on video boards

business_process: Venue management services for public owners (SL-2)
description: Operations, settlement reporting, and an owner portal for 8 publicly owned venues under management agreements
process_owner: Senior Vice President, Venue Management Services
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Owner agreements require monthly financial reporting and event settlement statements; owners rely on accurate revenue shares
manual_workaround: Email settlement statements prepared from ERP exports
dependent_systems: Settlement application and owner portal (Cloud B); SYS-08; SYS-01
quantified_impact_basis: Management fee credits and owner audit costs

description: Event announcements, presale codes, event change and cancellation notices by email, SMS, and app push (about 900 million messages a year)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cancellation and weather notices must reach ticket holders before doors; presale codes drive on-sale demand
manual_workaround: Post notices on the website, app banner, and social channels; contact center outbound for affected events
dependent_systems: SYS-10; SYS-05 (Cloud B customer data platform); SYS-01
dependent_third_parties: Email and SMS providers; app push notification services
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed announcements and presales (about $0.4 million) plus safety and refund risk when notices fail

description: Weekly payroll for about 7,900 part-time and seasonal staff and biweekly payroll for full-time staff (SOX-relevant)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll cutoff 72 hours before pay date; wage payment laws in 8 states; event staff retention
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll with adjustments through the payroll provider
quantified_impact_basis: Manual adjustments, penalties, and staffing shortfalls if event staff are paid late
acquired_venue_dependency: Yes: AV-01 to AV-06 employees move to the enterprise payroll on 2026-12-31

description: Quarterly and annual close, SOX controls, Form 10-Q and 10-K preparation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines at quarter-end (MTD drops to 48 hours in the close window); SOX IT general controls
manual_workaround: Extend the close calendar; manual journal entries with dual approval
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and audit fees; a late filing would be Severe

description: Artist offers, tour routing, holds, and marketing plans
process_owner: Chief Executive Officer (delegated to the President, Concerts)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Offers and holds run on multi-week cycles
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed offers; small risk of losing a tour date

business_process: Ticketing and POS operations at the acquired venues (AV-01 to AV-06)
description: Box office, stands, and venue IT at the 6 venues acquired on 2026-02-02 until migration to enterprise standards
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same event-day drivers as BP-05 and BP-06; legacy POS servers back up nightly to a local disk (actual RPO 24 hours) and have no tested restore
manual_workaround: Cash-free sales stop; sell through the app; manual will-call
dependent_systems: AV legacy POS servers and terminals; legacy directory; flat venue networks
dependent_third_parties: Legacy POS vendor; local IT support firm
quantified_impact_basis: About $0.35 million of event-day sales across the 6 venues on an average day
acquired_venue_dependency: Yes: AV-01 to AV-06 are the process
single_points_of_failure: Legacy POS server at each venue (single instance, no tested restore)
